identification: Victorian manuscript household and commonplace book in a full calf binding (blind and gilt ruled boards with fleuron corner tools, raised bands and fleurons on the spine), with an alphabetical cut thumb index down the fore-edge. Neat ink entries seen: 'Gooseberry Fool' recipe; a long 'Games' section of parlour games (Twenty Questions, Geography, Birds Beasts and Fishes, and others); a 'Galls ...' remedy; and a dated 'Gun Powder' entry (August 188?, reads as 1884) recording a trial of Curtis & Harvey's Diamond Grain black powder against White Schultze smokeless powder in a gun, with penetration figures. Loose items tucked in: a handwritten letter on blue-lined paper, a pencil landscape sketch of figures in a rural scene, a printed blue certificate or notice ('We hereby ...', signed), an envelope with a red stamp and postmarks, and other loose blue sheets. English household, about 1870-1890 judging by the hand, Curtis & Harvey and Schultze references. No owner name or place legible in the photos. Cloud scan is broadly right.

viewing_check: Flip through for an owner's name, a place or a date on the front pastedown or first leaf. Read the stamp and postmark on the envelope (a Tasmanian or other colonial cover could be worth more than the book). Read the blue printed certificate: who issued it, to whom, where. Count pages used.
